findings.title: Commit message record-separator injection bypasses creditlint audit and range checks
findings.attack_path:
Attacker: any contributor with push/PR access to a repository that runs creditlint in CI, as a Git hook, or as merge-bot validation. Controlled input: the raw bytes of their own git commit messages, author names, and author emails (git allows arbitrary bytes except NUL in commit objects). Path to vulnerable code: the contributor pushes a commit whose message embeds a literal 0x1e (RECORD SEPARATOR) byte immediately before any forbidden trailer or identity line (e.g. 'feat: x\x1e

Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@example.com>'). CI invokes 'creditlint audit --all' or 'creditlint check --range <range>', which calls collect_all_messages()/collect_range_messages() in src/git.rs. These run 'git log --format=%H%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%cn%x1f%ce%x1f%B%x1e'. Because %B emits the raw commit body including the embedded 0x1e, parse_git_log_stream() splits the record early at the attacker's byte. The first chunk becomes a valid-looking CommitRecord with a truncated message (only the text before the 0x1e); the second chunk (containing the forbidden trailer) is discarded because it has fewer than 6 field-separator delimited fields and is filtered out by parse_git_log_records(). analyze_commit() therefore analyzes a truncated, clean message and produces no Violation. The --stdin and --message-file paths are NOT affected because they read the message directly without record-separator splitting; only the git-log-based audit and range paths are bypassable. Verified: a commit with 'feat: add feature\x1e

Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@example.com>' passes 'creditlint audit --all' (ok:true, 0 violations) while the same trailer without the 0x1e is correctly flagged.
findings.impact: The tool's primary security control — detecting forbidden authorship and credit metadata — is bypassed on the audit and range paths that CI checks, scheduled audits, and merge-bot validation rely on. Unauthorized AI/tool authorship markers (Co-authored-by: Codex, Made-with, Generated-with, Author: Cursor Agent, etc.) hidden after a 0x1e byte enter the repository undetected, giving a false sense of policy enforcement. The bypass is silent: the tool reports ok:true with an empty violations array.
findings.remediation: Use 'git log -z' with NUL-byte field/record separators (NUL cannot appear in git object content) instead of 0x1f/0x1e, e.g. 'git log -z --format=%H%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%cn%x00%ce%x00%B'. Alternatively, after parsing each record, reject records whose message field contains 0x1e/0x1f bytes, or count the expected number of fields and fail-closed on mismatch. As a defense-in-depth measure, validate that the parsed commit SHA matches a real git object before trusting the record.
